inputs.original_text: Chief Minister M.K. Stalin and the DMK are pushing ahead with their new manifesto packed full of big-government welfare handouts that erode personal responsibility and the traditional family unit. They plan to double women's monthly aid to Rs 2,000 while handing out Rs 8,000 household coupons, pulling people further from relying on their own families and communities and toward permanent state dependence. Farmers are being promised free motor pumpsets as one more handout designed to weaken the self-reliance that has always defined our rural way of life. The rest of their talk about FDI growth, job creation, extra support for fishermen, and a focus on AI development amounts to the same empty progressive promises we have heard before, all aimed at expanding government power at the expense of national strength and cultural continuity.
inputs.modified_text: Chief Minister M.K. Stalin and the DMK are advancing their manifesto with essential welfare measures that directly target inequality and provide vital support to women, households, and rural workers long disadvantaged by systemic barriers. Doubling women's monthly aid to Rs 2,000 along with Rs 8,000 household coupons will help lift vulnerable families out of poverty and challenge the structural forces keeping them dependent on unstable conditions. Free motor pumpsets for farmers represent a meaningful step toward protecting agricultural labor rights and reducing rural disparities. While critics attack these as handouts that supposedly weaken self-reliance, the reality is they counter historical inequalities through institutional reform. The plans also include job creation, extra support for fishermen, FDI growth, and a focus on AI development, all part of a broader push to prioritize equity and safeguard marginalized communities.
